messages:
Ravi K.: Hey @people-ops, help needed — my sister's child is coming to live with me under a kinship care order from their home country. Can I add them to benefits now or do I have to wait for the passport/US court stuff?
Anya (People Ops): Welcome — congrats and thanks for flagging. Short answer: you can submit a QLE request now, but we need specific docs. Do you have the custody order scanned? :point_up:
Ravi K.: I have the foreign court order (PDF) and a birth certificate, but passport application is submitted and pending.
Megan (Benefits): Hi Ravi — we treat kinship/guardian additions similar to foster/adoption QLEs. Required docs usually: 1) custody/placement order, 2) proof of residency (utility or lease or school email), 3) birth cert or equivalent, and 4) ID when available. If the passport is delayed, we can provisionally accept the other docs and mark the dependent pending.
Ravi K.: Awesome. Does provisional acceptance change payroll deductions retroactively? I want to know if premiums will be adjusted back to the QLE date.
Megan (Benefits): Good Q. If the QLE is approved and you enroll within the 30-day window, coverage is effective back to the QLE event date (usually placement date). Payroll will be adjusted retroactively; PayrollBot will post adjustments in the next run.
Ravi K.: Is 30 days firm? The international courier messed up timing.
Anya (People Ops): 30 days is the standard window, but we can request an exception for documentation delays due to immigration or authority processing. Include a brief timeline and any courier receipts when you submit. Exception approvals are done by People Ops + Benefits lead.
Ravi K.: OK I'll upload: custody order (translated), birth cert, courier receipts, passport app confirmation, and a residency attestation from my landlord. Any special file naming or where to upload?
Megan (Benefits): Upload to our benefits portal -> "Manage Dependents" -> "Add Dependent (QLE)". For translations, include the original plus a certified English translation. File naming: lastname-dep-doctype (e.g., kiran-smith-custody-order.pdf) helps triage.
Anya (People Ops): Also add a short note in the submission: "Requesting provisional enrollment due to passport delay; documents attached; will provide passport when available." That flags it for expedited review.
Ravi K.: Thanks. How long does review usually take?
Megan (Benefits): We aim for 3 business days after complete submission. If you request an exception, it may take up to 5-7 business days. We'll ping you in-thread and mark the ticket.
PayrollBot: Payroll adjustment flag set: pending-review. Once People Ops confirms, a retro premium will be applied on the next payroll cycle.
Ravi K.: Perfect. One last thing — does this dependent count for FSA/HSA eligibility and dependent care?
Megan (Benefits): Yes, once enrolled as a dependent for medical/dental, they are eligible for dependent care FSA or HSA dependent considerations per plan rules. We can add specifics after approval.
Ravi K.: Great, uploading now. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
Anya (People Ops): Thanks Ravi — we'll watch for your submission and loop back. If anything urgent, DM me. :wave:
